data.title: Modernize pi integration: inherit main-session model/thinking, constrained sampling for structured_output, typed registerEntryRenderer, bash session-env tagging
data.executiveSummary: Adopt pi 0.82.x features as one cohesive change set across the pi-super-dev extension. The highest-leverage change makes every spawned specialist inherit the main session's model and thinking level (today extension.ts ignores ctx.model/ctx.thinkingLevel, so a user on Opus+xhigh gets role-default specialists). It also enables strict JSON-schema constrained sampling on the structured_output tool for capable providers (keeping the missingKeys corrective re-prompt as the fallback), removes the registerEntryRenderer capability cast now that it is typed in 0.82.1, and tags build-gate runs with pi's PI_SESSION_ID/PI_MODEL env vars for parallel-run correlation. All changes are additive, preserve the no-throw/best-effort discipline, and keep print/json/rpc/headless modes byte-clean.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: In src/extension.ts, inside the super_dev tool's execute(), ctx.model?.id and ctx.thinkingLevel are read BEFORE runPipelineTask(...) and threaded as DEFAULTS through RunOptions (e.g. inheritedModel / inheritedThinking) so that an explicit params.model or SUPER_DEV_MODEL / SUPER_DEV_THINKING env var still overrides them. Nothing throws when ctx.model / ctx.thinkingLevel are undefined (older or non-TUI ctx) — execution degrades to current behavior.

Model precedence is enforced end-to-end as: explicit params.model → SUPER_DEV_MODEL env (added to resolveModel if absent) → inherited ctx.model.id → SDK/settings default. The existing buildSpawnArgs behavior is preserved: --model is pushed only when a model is actually resolved.

resolveThinking() in src/pi-spawn.ts precedence chain is widened from (per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING env → role default) to (per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING env → INHERITED main-session ctx.thinkingLevel → role default). inheritedThinking is threaded through SpawnAgentOptions / SessionAgentOptions and from workflow.ts's realAgent (options.inheritedThinking).

In src/session-agent.ts runAgentViaSession, createAgentSession({ ... }) is given the resolved model via the SDK's model?: Model<any> option AND thinkingLevel directly as a createAgentSession option when an explicit-or-inherited value is available. applyThinkingLevel(session, ...) is retained as a second/best-effort line of defense but guarded against double-application. Note: model inheritance requires resolving ctx.model.id to a Model<any> — falls through to the SDK/settings default if the id cannot be resolved.

When super_dev is invoked WITHOUT explicit model/thinking params on a capable session, every spawned specialist on BOTH the session and subprocess backends uses the inherited model and a thinking level no LOWER than the role default would have been (inherited wins over role default; per-call/env still win). A new test asserts inheritedThinking flows from makeContext/realAgent into the agent call (e.g. a workflow test), and resolveThinking gets a precedence test covering the new inherited tier.

A small isStrictCapable(schema) helper is introduced (returns true only when the schema is a TSchema Object with at least one REQUIRED non-Optional key and additionalProperties: false). isStrictCapable is false for the current permissive controlSchema (all-Optional + additionalProperties: true) and for open/unknown-key schemas. It is unit-tested for required-keys, all-Optional, additionalProperties:true, and non-Object cases.

When the caller passes a real strict-capable schema (opts.schema) OR controlKeys can be built into a strict schema (Type.Object of required typed keys, additionalProperties: false), the structured_output tool (structuredOutputTool) sets constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" } — typed against the 0.82.1 ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling field. constrainedSampling is NEVER attached to a permissive schema (isStrictCapable gates it). The permissive Type.Optional(Type.Any()) + additionalProperties:true shape remains ONLY as the fallback for open/unknown-key schemas.

The missingKeys() + single corrective re-prompt turn machinery in session-agent.ts is PRESERVED unchanged as the fallback for non-capable providers (glm/local) and permissive schemas where strict constrained sampling is not applicable. A test asserts constrainedSampling is attached only when isStrictCapable(schema) is true (and absent otherwise — byte-identical behavior).

The registerEntryRenderer capability cast in src/extension.ts (const piWithRenderer = pi as unknown as {...}) is DELETED. activate() now calls pi.registerEntryRenderer(...) directly with the proper typed signature registerEntryRenderer<T>(customType: string, renderer: EntryRenderer<T>): void, importing EntryRenderer / EntryRenderOptions from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent where helpful. The existing try/catch best-effort guard and the durable background-summary transcript card rendering behavior are unchanged.

In the build gate (src/build-runner/gates.ts and/or its spawn path), when process.env.PI_SESSION_ID and/or process.env.PI_MODEL are present, the captured build-run log/trace/artifact metadata includes them (e.g. a correlation header line prepended/appended to the captured build log, or a field in any structured trace). When the env vars are absent the build run is byte-identical to today. Gate pass/fail logic and command construction are unchanged; a focused test covers present and absent cases.

CHANGELOG.md gains a concise [Unreleased] entry summarizing Features 1–4 (inherit main-session model/thinking; constrained sampling for structured_output; typed registerEntryRenderer; bash session-env tagging), noting the ^0.82.1 dependency bump is already done.
npm run typecheck is strict-clean against the 0.82.1 types, and the full vitest suite (existing 1437 tests + all new tests added for AC-05, AC-06, AC-08, AC-10) is green.

nonFunctional: No-throw / best-effort discipline: every new code path (reading ctx.model/ctx.thinkingLevel, resolving model to Model<any>, applying thinkingLevel, attaching constrainedSampling, reading PI_* env vars, registerEntryRenderer) must swallow failures and degrade to current behavior rather than abort a run.

Zero-ANSI byte-clean contract: print / json / rpc / headless modes must remain byte-identical — the dashboard widget, status pills, constrainedSampling header lines, and PI_* tagging must NOT emit ANSI or alter machine-readable output in those modes.

Additive-only, never-clobber: model/thinking inheritance must NEVER override an explicit user/LLM params.model, a SUPER_DEV_MODEL / SUPER_DEV_THINKING env var, or a per-call thinking override. Inheritance is a fallback tier only.

Strict JSON-schema correctness: constrainedSampling strict:"prefer" is requested ONLY on genuinely strict-capable schemas (required non-Optional keys + additionalProperties:false); never on permissive schemas to avoid provider no-ops or confusion.
Type safety: no new as unknown as casts; the registerEntryRenderer call uses the public 0.82.1 typed API and constrainedSampling is typed against ToolDefinition.
Observability-only change for Feature 4: PI_* tagging must not influence gate pass/fail, command construction, or timeout behavior; it only enriches captured build-run metadata.
openQuestions: Model inheritance (AC-04): ctx.model is a Model<any> with a string id, but createAgentSession's model option expects a Model<any> (not just an id string). Should the inherited model be passed by re-using ctx.model directly (the live Model instance) when available, or by resolving ctx.model.id back to a Model via the SDK's model registry? Re-using ctx.model is simplest and avoids a registry round-trip, but the task text mentions ctx.model.id — confirm the preferred source.

ConstrainedSampling fallback semantics (AC-07): on a capable provider with strict:"prefer" that the model cannot honor, does pi silently fall back to normal tool calling (so missingKeys still fires), or could it raise? The AC assumes graceful fallback; verify against pi 0.82.1 runtime behavior for at least one capable provider.

Feature 4 location: the build gate (src/build-runner/gates.ts) currently returns structured results (stdout/stderr) rather than writing a trace file to disk. Is the intended 'build-run log/trace/artifact' the captured gate stdout/stderr that flows into the live transcript + run log (via sink.log), a dedicated on-disk build trace, or both? Confirm where the correlation header should be injected so it is observable without altering gate logic.

data.title: pi 0.82.x SDK modernization: model/thinking inheritance, constrained sampling for structured_output, typed registerEntryRenderer, and PI_* build-tagging
data.summary: Research against the pi 0.82.0/0.82.1 primary sources (repo CHANGELOG, pi-ai README, extensions.md, sdk.md, environment-variables.md, and the structured-output & custom-model SDK examples) confirms every required API is public and typed in the bumped 0.82.1 surface. Feature 1: createAgentSession({ model, thinkingLevel, modelRuntime }) accepts a resolved Model<any> AND a thinkingLevel as first-class creation options (canonical path); ctx.model is a live Model<any> with .id/.provider and ctx.modelRegistry can resolve ids via getModel(provider,id) (built-in) or modelRuntime.getModel() (incl. custom). Feature 2: ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling is typed false | { type:'json_schema'; strict:'prefer'|'require' } | { type:'grammar'; variants:{...} }; strict:'prefer' uses provider strict enforcement when supported and SILENTLY falls back to normal tool calling otherwise (verified via pi-ai's resolveStrictSampling: unsupported+'prefer' returns undefined, no throw; unsupported+'require' throws) — so missingKeys() is correctly retained as the fallback. Strict-capable JSON schema = object with required keys + additionalProperties:false (OpenAI & pi examples align); Optional keys and additionalProperties:true must NOT request strict. Feature 3: registerEntryRenderer<T>(customType, renderer) is public typed API in 0.82.1; EntryRenderer/EntryRenderOptions are exported from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Feature 4: PI_SESSION_ID/PI_SESSION_FILE/PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL are injected into commands run by built-in/factory bash tools; values are resolved at command start, absent in user !/!! commands and SDK-embedded runs — read process.env defensively. Open Questions 1 and 2 are resolved; Question 3 (exact injection point) is a codebase-internal decision the research bounds but cannot finalize.

options.name: Feature 1 — Thread the live ctx.model as the primary inherited Model, resolve ctx.model.id via getModel/modelRuntime only as fallback (AC-01/02/04/08)
options.tradeoffs: createAgentSession's model option expects a Model<any> instance, not an id string (sdk.md + 02-custom-model.ts). Simplest, no registry round-trip: when ctx.model is a live Model<any>, thread that instance directly through RunOptions (e.g. inheritedModel as Model<any> OR a resolved id + re-resolution at the session boundary). If the option chain must carry a string id (per AC-04 'resolve ctx.model.id to Model<any>'), resolve it at runAgentViaSession using getModel(provider,id) for built-ins (no auth check, synchronous, from @earendil-works/pi-ai) or modelRuntime.getModel(provider,id) to include custom models — both confirmed in sdk.md. Risk: getModel only knows built-ins; custom/proxy models need modelRuntime, which must be threaded in. Recommendation: thread ctx.model.id as the inherited string, and resolve to Model<any> at the session-creation boundary with a getModel→modelRuntime→undefined fallback that degrades to the SDK/settings default (never throws). Precedence explicit-param → SUPER_DEV_MODEL env → inherited id → SDK default is preserved by treating inherited as the lowest-priority non-default tier.

options.name: Feature 1 — thinkingLevel: pass it as a createAgentSession option (canonical) and keep applyThinkingLevel() guarded as best-effort second defense (AC-03/04/07)
options.tradeoffs: sdk.md shows createAgentSession({ thinkingLevel: 'medium' }) and session.setThinkingLevel(level) as the supported, clamped path (values: off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max; clamped to model capabilities). Passing thinkingLevel in createAgentSession options is the canonical single-application point. Keeping the existing applyThinkingLevel(session,...) as best-effort is reasonable for older runtimes BUT must be guarded against double-application (if the option already set it, skip or compare current level before re-applying). Recommendation: set thinkingLevel in createAgentSession when an explicit-or-inherited value exists; guard applyThinkingLevel to only fire when session.thinkingLevel !== resolved level. Widened resolveThinking precedence (per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING env → inherited ctx.thinkingLevel → role default) feeds this resolved value.

options.name: Feature 2 — Use strict:'prefer' (never 'require') and gate on isStrictCapable(schema) = Object + >=1 required non-Optional key + additionalProperties:false (AC-06/07/08)
options.tradeoffs: pi-ai README: strict:'prefer' enforces provider-side strict schema when supported and otherwise falls back to normal tool calling (resolveStrictSampling returns undefined, no throw); strict:'require' FAILS the request when unsupported. Since missingKeys()+corrective re-prompt is the deliberate fallback for non-capable providers (glm/local) and permissive schemas, 'prefer' is the only safe choice — it never raises and never breaks a run. OpenAI/pi strict requirements (OpenAI structured-outputs guide + pi edit_file/grammar examples) mandate an object schema, ALL relevant keys required (Optional emulated via type:["string","null"]), and additionalProperties:false at every object level. So isStrictCapable must return false for the current permissive controlSchema (all-Optional + additionalProperties:true) and for non-Object schemas — exactly AC-06. Build the strict variant as Type.Object({...required typed keys...}, { additionalProperties:false }) and attach constrainedSampling only when isStrictCapable is true; byte-identical behavior otherwise.

options.name: Feature 3 — Call pi.registerEntryRenderer(customType, renderer) directly (typed); import EntryRenderer/EntryRenderOptions from the package root (AC-09/SCENARIO-014/015)
options.tradeoffs: Confirmed in the real pi repo's extensions index.ts that EntryRenderer, EntryRenderOptions, and ToolDefinition are re-exported from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. registerEntryRenderer<T>(customType: string, renderer: EntryRenderer<T>): void is the public typed 0.82.1 signature (the prior as-unknown-as cast existed only because it was absent in 0.80.3). Delete the cast and the piWithRenderer shim; keep the existing try/catch best-effort guard (SCENARIO-015) and the durable background-summary transcript-card rendering. typecheck stays strict-clean because the types now resolve against the bumped ^0.82.1 surface.

options.name: Feature 4 — Read process.env.PI_SESSION_ID / PI_MODEL defensively and inject a correlation header/field into build-gate captured output only when present (AC-10/SCENARIO-016/017)
options.tradeoffs: environment-variables.md confirms PI_SESSION_ID/PI_SESSION_FILE/PI_PROVIDER/PI_MODEL/PI_REASONING_LEVEL are injected into commands run by built-in and factory-created bash tools (resolved at command start; absent for user !/!! commands and SDK-embedded runs). These vars are inherited by the build-gate's child processes, so reading process.env in build-runner is valid and never throws. To keep print/json/rpc/headless modes byte-clean, add the correlation data as a structured metadata field or a clearly-delimited header line that is emitted ONLY when the vars are present (absent → byte-identical to today). Recommendation: a single guarded 'PI_SESSION_ID=… PI_MODEL=…' correlation line/field appended to the captured build log or a structured-trace field; gate pass/fail and command construction must be untouched (observability-only).

openIssues: RESOLVED (was OQ-1, model inheritance source): createAgentSession.model expects a Model<any> instance. The live ctx.model can be threaded directly (simplest) OR its .id resolved via getModel(provider,id) (built-ins, sync, no auth check) / modelRuntime.getModel(provider,id) (incl. custom). If RunOptions carries a string inheritedModel per AC-04, resolution must happen at the session boundary with getModel→modelRuntime→undefined fallback so it never throws (SCENARIO-008). Implementation-stage detail: whether to thread the Model instance or the id string through RunOptions is a codebase call; research confirms both paths are supported.

RESOLVED (was OQ-2, constrainedSampling fallback): pi-ai's resolveStrictSampling shows strict:'prefer' returns undefined (normal tool-calling fallback, no throw) when the provider/model cannot honor it; only strict:'require' throws. So missingKeys()+corrective re-prompt remains the correct fallback and will still fire on non-capable providers (glm/local) and permissive schemas. Use 'prefer' exclusively.

STILL AMBIGUOUS (was OQ-3, Feature 4 injection point): research confirms the PI_* env vars exist and are inherited by build-gate child processes, but whether to inject a correlation line into captured stdout/stderr (flows through sink.log → live transcript + run log) vs a dedicated structured-trace field is a codebase-internal decision requiring inspection of build-runner/gates.ts result shape. The byte-clean + observability-only constraints bound it to: emit only when vars present, never touch pass/fail or command construction. Recommend the next stage inspect gates.ts to choose header-line vs structured-field so machine-readable modes stay byte-identical.

MINOR (verify in repo): ctx.thinkingLevel availability on the super_dev tool's execute() ctx. Research confirms ctx.model is on ExtensionContext and thinkingLevel_select events carry levels, and pi.getThinkingLevel()/session.thinkingLevel exist; the requirement asserts ctx.thinkingLevel is readable in the tool ctx. If the tool-execute ctx lacks a thinkingLevel field, fall back to reading it via the session/runtime accessor — implementation stage should confirm the exact ctx shape (no-throw if undefined, per SCENARIO-002).

data.title: Codebase Assessment: pi-integration-modernization (pi-super-dev)
data.summary: pi-super-dev is an ESM TypeScript *pi-extension* package (not a standalone app — it runs INSIDE the `pi` agent). The change set modernizes the pi integration on the already-bumped `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@^0.82.1` / `@earendil-works/pi-tui@^0.82.1` / `typebox@1.1.38` toolchain. Architecture: `extension.ts` registers the `super_dev` tool + `/super-dev` command + entry renderer; `pipeline.ts` → `workflow.ts` (the `realAgent` seam) → a two-backend specialist layer (`pi-spawn.ts` subprocess vs `session-agent.ts` in-process `createAgentSession`); control-flow node algebra in `nodes.ts` (DO NOT TOUCH). The dominant, load-bearing convention is **no-throw best-effort**: every capability is try/catch-guarded or feature-detected, precedence chains are documented verbatim in JSDoc, and a single shared `common` options object is threaded to BOTH backends so additive option fields propagate for free. The implementation is low-risk: it mirrors an already-established 4-step precedence resolver (`resolveThinking`) and an already-existing additive option pattern; the only genuinely new surface is `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling` (0.82.0) and the typed `registerEntryRenderer`. There is NO API/UI server to bring up — verification is `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` (vitest), both already green (1437 tests).

data.title: Technical Specification: pi Integration Modernization — Main-Session Model/Thinking Inheritance, Constrained Sampling for structured_output, Typed registerEntryRenderer, and Bash Session-Env Build Tagging
data.summary: Modernize the pi-super-dev pi-extension on the already-bumped `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@^0.82.1` toolchain in five cohesive, independently-shippable changes. (1) HIGHEST leverage: every spawned specialist inherits the live main session's model + thinking level, threaded as additive `inheritedModel`/`inheritedThinking` DEFAULTS through the existing option chain (extension.execute → RunOptions → realAgent.common → both backends), with explicit params and SUPER_DEV_* env still winning and a widened `resolveThinking`/model precedence chain. (2) Adopt pi 0.82.0 `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` on the `structured_output` tool, gated by a small `isStrictCapable(schema)` helper, while keeping `missingKeys()` + the single corrective re-prompt as the non-capable-provider/permissive-schema fallback. (3) Delete the `registerEntryRenderer` `as unknown as` capability cast now that it is typed on the 0.82.1 public API. (4) Tag build-gate runs with pi's `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_MODEL` env vars for parallel-run correlation (observability-only). (5) CHANGELOG. Every change preserves the load-bearing no-throw/best-effort discipline and the print/json/rpc/headless zero-ANSI byte-clean contract; all changes are additive and never clobber an explicit user/LLM/env override. Verification is `npm run typecheck` strict-clean + the full vitest suite (1437 + new tests) green.
data.architecture:
pi-super-dev is an ESM TypeScript *pi-extension* package that runs INSIDE the `pi` agent and executes a 13-stage dev pipeline by spawning specialist `pi` agents. The change set is layered across the existing specialist-execution architecture without touching the control-flow node algebra (`nodes.ts`), the resume cache, or the pipeline stage structure.

SPECIALIST EXECUTION SEAM. The architecture to extend is: `extension.ts` registers the `super_dev` tool + `/super-dev` command; its `execute()` calls `runPipelineTask(task, {...})` (`pipeline.ts`) which carries a single `RunOptions` object (src/types.ts) down to `makeContext`/`realAgent` in `workflow.ts`. `realAgent` builds ONE shared `common` options object and dispatches to one of TWO backends: `spawnAgent` (`pi-spawn.ts`, raw `pi` subprocess, NDJSON stdout, `<control>` text) or `runAgentViaSession` (`session-agent.ts`, in-process `createAgentSession`, schema-validated `structured_output` tool). The `common` object deliberately carries cross-backend fields (e.g. `controlKeys` "Ignored by the subprocess backend … so the same common options object can feed both backends"), so ADDITIVE option fields propagate to both backends for free — this is the core seam for Feature 1.

FEATURE 1 — MODEL/THINKING INHERITANCE (the load-bearing change). Today `extension.execute()` never reads `ctx.model` / `ctx.thinkingLevel`, so specialists resolve model and thinking independently (explicit param → SUPER_DEV_* env → role default). The fix threads two additive DEFAULTS — `inheritedModel?: string` and `inheritedThinking?: ThinkingLevel` — through the full chain: (a) capture `ctx.model?.id` and `ctx.thinkingLevel` defensively (optional chaining; never throw on older/non-TUI ctx) inside `execute()` BEFORE `runPipelineTask(...)` and pass them as `inheritedModel`/`inheritedThinking` in the options; (b) add both fields to `RunOptions` (additive, optional); (c) forward them from `realAgent`'s `common` object; (d) `SpawnAgentOptions`/`SessionAgentOptions` gain the same additive fields. THINKING: widen `resolveThinking(agent, perCall?, inherited?)` precedence to `per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING env → INHERITED (ctx.thinkingLevel) → role default`, and resolve thinking ONCE so the session backend does not double-apply. MODEL: precedence `explicit opts.model → SUPER_DEV_MODEL env (NEW) → inherited ctx.model.id → SDK/settings default`, preserving the existing `buildSpawnArgs` rule that `--model` is pushed ONLY when a model resolves. Session backend: pass the resolved model via `createAgentSession({ model, thinkingLevel })` (the canonical 0.82.x option path) as a SECOND line of defense alongside the retained best-effort `applyThinkingLevel(session, …)`, guarded against double-application. Inheritance is ADDITIVE-only — it never overrides an explicit `params.model`, a `SUPER_DEV_MODEL`/`SUPER_DEV_THINKING` env var, or a per-call override; older ctx (no model/thinking) degrades byte-identically to today.

FEATURE 2 — CONSTRAINED SAMPLING. `session-agent.ts` carries a structured-output workaround (`controlSchema(keys)` declares keys as `Optional(Type.Any())` with `additionalProperties: true`; `missingKeys()` + a single corrective re-prompt turn self-heal partial fills) precisely because models do not reliably fill schemas. pi 0.82.0 added `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling?: false | { type: "json_schema"; strict: "prefer" | "require" }`. The fix introduces a strict-capable schema variant (`Type.Object({ …required typed keys… }, { additionalProperties: false })`) and a small `isStrictCapable(schema)` helper (true ONLY for a typebox Object with ≥1 required non-Optional key AND `additionalProperties === false`). `structuredOutputTool` sets `constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` ONLY when `isStrictCapable` holds (typed against the 0.82.1 `ToolDefinition`); it is NEVER attached to a permissive schema (the current all-Optional controlSchema, or any open/unknown-key schema), avoiding provider no-ops/confusion. The permissive controlSchema + `missingKeys()` corrective re-prompt machinery is PRESERVED byte-identical as the fallback for non-capable providers (glm/local) and permissive schemas — strict `prefer` falls back to normal tool calling there, so the corrective path still earns its keep.

FEATURE 3 — TYPED registerEntryRenderer (pure cleanup). `extension.ts` casts `pi as unknown as { registerEntryRenderer?: … }` because the method was absent from the pinned 0.80.3 type surface. As of 0.82.1 it is public on `ExtensionAPI`: `registerEntryRenderer<T>(customType: string, renderer: EntryRenderer<T>): void`. The cast is deleted and `pi.registerEntryRenderer("super-dev-summary", …)` is called directly with proper types (importing `EntryRenderer`/`EntryRenderOptions` from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` where helpful), keeping the existing try/catch best-effort guard and the durable background-summary transcript-card rendering.

FEATURE 4 — BASH SESSION-ENV TAGGING (observability-only). pi 0.82.0 exposes `PI_SESSION_ID`, `PI_SESSION_FILE`, `PI_PROVIDER`, `PI_MODEL`, `PI_REASONING_LEVEL` to commands run by built-in bash tools. `build-runner/gates.ts` `runBuildGate`/`BuildGateResult` capture build/test/typecheck stdout/stderr. The fix reads `process.env.PI_SESSION_ID` and `process.env.PI_MODEL` DEFENSIVELY and, when present, includes them as a plain-ASCII correlation tag in the captured build-run metadata (a `# pi-session=<id> model=<model>` header line and/or an additive `correlation?: { sessionId?: string; model?: string }` field on `BuildGateResult`). No-throw when absent; byte-identical when absent; does NOT alter gate pass/fail logic, command construction, or timeout behavior.

CROSS-CUTTING CONTRACTS. (1) No-throw/best-effort: every new capability read (ctx.model/thinking, model-id→Model resolution, createAgentSession options, constrainedSampling gating, PI_* env reads, registerEntryRenderer) is try/catch-guarded or feature-detected and degrades to current behavior. (2) Zero-ANSI byte-clean for print/json/rpc/headless: all new output (PI_* correlation tags, constrainedSampling is tool metadata not output) is plain ASCII with no control codes and touches no rendering in non-TUI modes. (3) Type safety: no new `as unknown as` casts; constrainedSampling typed against `ToolDefinition`; registerEntryRenderer uses the public typed API.

data.title: Spec Review: pi Integration Modernization (05-specification.md)
data.summary: Fagan-style content inspection of the pi Integration Modernization specification across 8 dimensions. The spec is exceptionally well-grounded: I verified 11 distinct code/API claims against the actual worktree and the installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.82.1 type surface, and all 11 check out (grounding score 100%, well above the 90% HIGH bar). Confirmed: ^0.82.1 is committed in package.json peerDependencies; resolveThinking(agent, perCall?) exists at src/pi-spawn.ts:150 with the exact precedence the spec widens; controlSchema is all-Optional + additionalProperties:true at session-agent.ts:172; missingKeys + the structuredOutputTool schema-fallback exist; the `pi as unknown as { registerEntryRenderer? }` cast exists at extension.ts:656; BuildGateResult exists at build-runner/gates.ts:91; `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling?: false | ConstrainedSamplingConfig` IS in the 0.82.1 types (extensions/types.d.ts:351); the typed public `registerEntryRenderer<T>(customType, renderer)` IS on ExtensionAPI (types.d.ts:903); createAgentSession options carry thinkingLevel/model; and PI_SESSION_ID/PI_MODEL are present in the 0.82.x bash tool runtime. All 12 ACs (AC-01..12) and all 20 BDD scenarios (SCENARIO-001..020) map cleanly to spec sections via the 5 phases, so the blocking coverage/traceability gate passes. The defects found are Medium/Low ambiguity issues concentrated in Feature 1's session-backend Model-object resolution and Feature 4's dual correlation representation — none are hallucinated references, infeasible architecture, or broken traceability. No critical, no high findings. Verdict: APPROVED WITH REVISIONS.

findings.title: Feature 1: model-id → Model-object resolution for the session backend is unspecified
findings.detail: Feature 1 threads the inherited value as `ctx.model?.id` (a string) and says the session backend passes 'the resolved model via `createAgentSession({ model, thinkingLevel })`'. But createAgentSession's `model` option is typed `Model<any>` (agent-session.d.ts:168 `model: Model<any>`), NOT a string. The subprocess backend can take a bare id via `--model <id>`, but the in-process session backend must resolve the string id to a Model object. The spec's cross-cutting contracts mention 'model-id→Model resolution' as a no-throw capability but never name the resolution API (SDK model registry / getModel), where it is invoked, or its no-throw failure mode. SCENARIO-002/008 reference a 'model-id-cannot-resolve fall-through' yet the spec body defines neither the resolver nor its behavior. Recommendation: name the resolution function and specify that an unresolvable id degrades to the SDK/settings default (byte-identical to today) rather than throwing.

findings.title: Feature 4: 'header line AND/OR correlation field' is an unresolved internal inconsistency
findings.detail: Feature 4 specifies the correlation tag as 'a `# pi-session=<id> model=<model>` header line AND/OR an additive `correlation?: { sessionId?: string; model?: string }` field on BuildGateResult'. These are two materially different representations with different testability and byte-clean profiles. The Testing Strategy then asserts 'the correlation tag appears in captured output' (SCENARIO-016/017), which is only satisfiable by the header-line approach — a structured field on the result object would NOT appear in 'captured output'. The 'and/or' leaves the implementer to guess and makes SCENARIO-016/017 untestable as written if the field-only path is chosen. Recommendation: pick ONE canonical representation (header line, to satisfy the stated scenario) OR split into two scenarios with distinct assertions.

findings.title: Feature 1: 'resolve thinking ONCE / no double-apply' guard mechanism not specified
findings.detail: Feature 1 asserts thinking is resolved ONCE and the retained best-effort `applyThinkingLevel` is 'guarded against double-application' alongside `createAgentSession({ thinkingLevel })`, and the Testing Strategy demands a test that 'applyThinkingLevel does not double-apply'. But the concrete guard is left to the implementer (e.g. skip applyThinkingLevel when thinkingLevel was passed to createAgentSession, vs. make createAgentSession authoritative and applyThinkingLevel a no-op, vs. a flag). The test asserts a behavior the spec never defines. Recommendation: state the precedence explicitly (e.g. 'when thinkingLevel is passed to createAgentSession, applyThinkingLevel is skipped').

findings.title: Feature 2: isStrictCapable relies on typebox Optional introspection that is not pinned
findings.detail: `isStrictCapable(schema)` is defined as 'true ONLY for a typebox Object with ≥1 required non-Optional key AND additionalProperties === false'. In typebox 1.x (peer dep ^1.1.0), detecting a 'non-Optional' key requires inspecting the `[OptionalKind]` Symbol modifier on each property — a version-dependent, finicky introspection. The spec does not name the typebox guard API (e.g. TypeGuard.TObject + OptionalKind symbol check) the helper must use. The behavioral test cases (required+additionalProperties:false → true, all-Optional → false, additionalProperties:true → false, non-Object → false) pin behavior but not the implementation path. Recommendation: cite the specific typebox introspection so the helper is implementable without reverse-engineering.

findings.title: AC-12 / Testing Strategy: hardcoded '1437 tests' baseline is brittle and unverifiable from the spec
findings.detail: The spec, requirements, and task-list all assert 'existing 1437 tests' as fact (AC-12). This number is plausible (78 test files) but is not confirmable from the spec itself and will drift on the first unrelated test addition, silently invalidating the cited baseline. AC-12's actual gate ('full vitest suite green') does not depend on the exact count. Recommendation: phrase as 'the existing vitest suite' or mark the count as approximate/as-of a commit, to avoid a false-failure impression when the number inevitably changes.

findings.title: Feature 2: constrainedSampling strict='prefer' provider-coverage rationale uncited
findings.detail: Feature 2 chooses `strict: 'prefer'` and relies on the pi-internal contract that non-capable providers fall back to normal tool calling (it names 'glm/local' as non-capable) so the missingKeys corrective re-prompt still earns its keep. This fallback behavior is a pi-internal guarantee the spec depends on but does not cite a source for. The design degrades safely regardless, so impact is low, but the choice of 'prefer' over 'require' is only justified by this unstated contract. Recommendation: cite the pi behavior (or note that 'prefer' is chosen precisely because the design must not break non-capable providers).

dimensions.name: D1 Completeness
dimensions.notes: 4/5. All 12 ACs (AC-01..12) have a spec section and all 20 BDD scenarios (SCENARIO-001..020) are addressed via the 5-phase decomposition. Error handling is pervasively specified (no-throw/best-effort). NFRs (byte-clean zero-ANSI, type-safety, no new casts) covered. Gap: the Model-object resolution path for the session backend (F-1) and the double-apply guard (F-3) are referenced but not defined.

dimensions.name: D2 Consistency
dimensions.notes: 4/5. Names are uniform across sections (inheritedModel/inheritedThinking, resolveThinking precedence tiers, controlSchema/missingKeys/isStrictCapable, BuildGateResult/correlation). The one inconsistency is the Feature 4 'header line AND/OR correlation field' dual representation (F-2), which conflicts with its own SCENARIO-016/017 assertion.

dimensions.name: D3 Feasibility
dimensions.notes: 4/5. Architecture fits the established two-backend specialist seam; additive option threading mirrors the existing resolveThinking pattern; constrainedSampling and registerEntryRenderer both confirmed present on the 0.82.1 public type surface. Feasibility nuance: createAgentSession wants a Model<any>, not a string id (F-1); isStrictCapable depends on typebox-1.x Symbol introspection (F-4).

dimensions.name: D4 Testability
dimensions.notes: 4/5. ACs are measurable; the Testing Strategy maps each phase to concrete unit tests (precedence tiers, isStrictCapable truth table, requireNotContains cast removal, env-set/unset build-tag, CHANGELOG requireContains). Thresholds are mostly behavioral rather than numeric, which is appropriate for a no-output-change refactor. Weak spots: SCENARIO-016/017 assertion depends on the unresolved header-vs-field choice (F-2); 'no double-apply' test asserts unspecified behavior (F-3).

dimensions.name: D5 Traceability
dimensions.notes: 5/5. Unbroken chains: AC-01..05→Feature 1→SCENARIO-001..008; AC-06,07,08→Feature 2→SCENARIO-009..013; AC-09→Feature 3→SCENARIO-014,015; AC-10→Feature 4→SCENARIO-016,017; AC-11→Feature 5→SCENARIO-018; AC-12→cross-cutting→SCENARIO-019,020. The BDD Scenario References section lists all 20; phase data confirms the mapping. Phase ordering (1 before 2/3/4; 5 last) is consistent with shared-file dependencies.

dimensions.name: D6 Grounding
dimensions.notes: 5/5 — 100% (11/11 claims verified). ^0.82.1 committed (package.json); resolveThinking@pi-spawn.ts:150; controlSchema@session-agent.ts:172; missingKeys@session-agent.ts:179; structuredOutputTool schema fallback@session-agent.ts:241; registerEntryRenderer cast@extension.ts:656; BuildGateResult@gates.ts:91; constrainedSampling field@extensions/types.d.ts:351; typed registerEntryRenderer<T>@types.d.ts:903; createAgentSession model/thinkingLevel options@agent-session.d.ts; PI_SESSION_ID/PI_MODEL in bash runtime. No hallucinated references. The single source-unverified claim is the constrainedSampling 'prefer' provider-fallback contract (F-6).

dimensions.name: D7 Complexity
dimensions.notes: 5/5. Five small, independently-shippable, additive changes touching a bounded file set (extension.ts, types.ts, workflow.ts, pi-spawn.ts, session-agent.ts, build-runner/gates.ts, CHANGELOG.md). No new abstractions beyond a tiny isStrictCapable helper; no gold-plating; explicitly preserves the control-flow node algebra and resume cache untouched. Simplest viable approach for each feature.

dimensions.name: D8 Ambiguity
dimensions.notes: 3/5. Several load-bearing behaviors are named but not defined: (a) Feature 4 header-vs-field representation (F-2); (b) Feature 1 Model-object resolution + no-throw failure mode (F-1); (c) Feature 1 double-apply guard mechanism (F-3); (d) Feature 2 typebox Optional-introspection path (F-4). State transitions (precedence tiers) ARE explicit, error responses (no-throw) ARE specified, defaults ARE stated. Resolving the four ambiguity findings would raise this to 4-5.

data.title: pi Integration Modernization (spec-15) — model/thinking inheritance, constrained structured_output sampling, typed registerEntryRenderer, bash session-env build tagging
data.summary:
Cohesive adoption of pi 0.82.x features across the pi-super-dev extension as four additive, no-throw/best-effort changes plus a CHANGELOG entry. Built on the already-committed `^0.82.1` `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` bump; zero new runtime dependencies.

## What was built, by phase

**Phase 1 — Inherit main-session model + thinking level (Feature 1; AC-01..05; SCENARIO-001..008).** The core, prerequisite change. `extension.execute()` now defensively captures `ctx.model?.id` / `ctx.thinkingLevel` (optional chaining; never throws on older/non-TUI ctx) BEFORE `runPipelineTask(...)` and threads additive `inheritedModel?: string` / `inheritedThinking?: ThinkingLevel` DEFAULTS through the full specialist chain: `RunOptions` (src/types.ts) → `realAgent.common` (src/workflow.ts) → BOTH the `pi`-subprocess backend (`SpawnAgentOptions` in src/pi-spawn.ts) and the in-process `createAgentSession` backend (src/session-agent.ts).
- `resolveThinking` precedence widened to `per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING env → INHERITED (ctx.thinkingLevel) → role default`.
- Model resolution added: `explicit params.model → SUPER_DEV_MODEL env (NEW) → inherited ctx.model.id → SDK/settings default`; `--model` pushed only when a model resolves.
- Session backend passes `model`/`thinkingLevel` as `createAgentSession({...})` options alongside the retained best-effort `applyThinkingLevel`, guarded against double-application (skipped when thinkingLevel already passed to createAgentSession — resolves spec-review F-3).
- Explicit params and SUPER_DEV_* env always win (additive, never clobber); unresolvable model id degrades to SDK/settings default rather than throwing (resolves F-1).

**Phase 2 — Constrained tool sampling for structured_output (Feature 2; AC-06,07,08; SCENARIO-009..013).** Localized to src/session-agent.ts. New `isStrictCapable(schema)` helper (true ONLY for a typebox Object with ≥1 required non-Optional key AND `additionalProperties === false`) gates a new strict-capable schema variant; `structuredOutputTool` sets `constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` on the `ToolDefinition` ONLY when `isStrictCapable` holds, typed against the 0.82.1 `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling` field. NEVER attached to the permissive controlSchema. `missingKeys()` + the single corrective re-prompt turn preserved byte-identical as the non-capable-provider / permissive-schema fallback.

**Phase 3 — Typed registerEntryRenderer (Feature 3; AC-09; SCENARIO-014,015).** Pure cleanup in src/extension.ts. Deleted `const piWithRenderer = pi as unknown as {…}`; `activate()` now calls `pi.registerEntryRenderer("super-dev-summary", …)` directly against the public 0.82.1 typed signature, importing `EntryRenderer`/`EntryRenderOptions`. Best-effort try/catch wrapper and durable background-summary transcript-card rendering unchanged. No new `as unknown as` casts.

**Phase 4 — Tag build runs with pi session-env vars (Feature 4; AC-10; SCENARIO-016,017).** src/build-runner/gates.ts `runBuildGate` defensively reads `process.env.PI_SESSION_ID` / `process.env.PI_MODEL`; when at least one is present, stamps an additive `correlation?: { sessionId?: string; model?: string }` field onto `BuildGateResult`. Field is OMITTED entirely (byte-identical to today) when both are absent. Read is try-guarded so a hostile env proxy cannot stall the gate. Observability-only: no pass/fail, command-construction, or timeout change; plain ASCII, no control codes.

**Phase 5 — CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry (Feature 5; AC-11; SCENARIO-018).** Appended a Keep-a-Changelog bold-leading-bullet entry to CHANGELOG.md summarizing Features 1–4 and noting the ^0.82.1 bump is already committed. Matches the prior `[Unreleased]` entry style.

## Files changed (15)

Source: src/extension.ts, src/session-agent.ts, src/pi-spawn.ts, src/workflow.ts, src/types.ts, src/build-runner/gates.ts. Docs: CHANGELOG.md. Tests (8, all new or extended): tests/extension-inherit.test.ts, tests/session-agent-inherit.test.ts, tests/workflow-inherit.test.ts, tests/pi-spawn.test.ts, tests/session-agent-constrained-sampling.test.ts, tests/extension-entry-renderer.test.ts, tests/build-runner-correlation.test.ts, tests/changelog-unreleased-spec15.test.ts. Net +1544/−37 across 15 files; 5 commits (`59721185`…`5fbf7213`).

## Test results

`npm run typecheck` strict-clean against the 0.82.1 type surface (no new `as unknown as` casts). Full vitest suite green. New coverage: resolveThinking INHERITED-precedence tier, inheritedThinking flow from realAgent/makeContext into the spawned agent call, isStrictCapable truth table (required-keys/all-Optional/additionalProperties:true/non-Object) + gated constrainedSampling attach/absent, registerEntryRenderer cast removal (require-not-contains `as unknown as`), build-gate correlation present/absent env cases, and the CHANGELOG entry contract (four anchors + ^0.82.1 note + preservation of prior entries).

## Deviations / spec-review resolutions

- F-1 (Model-object resolution): implemented the no-throw fall-through — unresolvable inherited model id degrades to the SDK/settings default rather than throwing; documented in code comments.
- F-2 (header-line AND/OR field ambiguity): settled on the additive `correlation` field representation; tests assert it is populated when env set and absent (byte-identical) when unset.
- F-3 (double-apply guard): applyThinkingLevel skipped when thinkingLevel already passed to createAgentSession; precedence made explicit.
- F-4/F-6 (isStrictCapable introspection / strict:"prefer" rationale): behavioral test cases pin the helper; "prefer" chosen to keep non-capable providers (glm/local) on the normal tool-call path so missingKeys still fires.
- F-5 (brittle '1437 tests' baseline): treated as approximate; AC-12 gate is the full vitest suite being green, not a fixed count.
All non-functional requirements honored: additive-only, no-throw/best-effort, zero-ANSI byte-clean print/json/rpc/headless modes, no new runtime deps, type-safe (no new casts).

data.title: Adversarial Review — SPEC-15 pi Integration Modernization (model/thinking inheritance, constrained sampling, typed registerEntryRenderer, bash session-env build tagging)
data.summary:
All five phases landed as one cohesive, strictly-additive, no-throw change set. Feature 1's precedence widening is correct and symmetric in the common case; Feature 2's `isStrictCapable` gate correctly keeps the permissive path byte-identical; Feature 3 cleanly deletes the `as unknown as` cast; Feature 4 is observability-only and byte-identical when env vars are absent; CHANGELOG is present. I confirmed against the pinned 0.82.1 d.ts that every new API touch (`ModelRuntime.create/getModel/getModels`, `createAgentSession({ model, thinkingLevel })`, `ToolDefinition.constrainedSampling`, `EntryRenderer`/`registerEntryRenderer`) is genuinely typed and exported — typecheck claims are credible. The Destructive Action Gate is clean (no DROP/DELETE-without-WHERE/rm -rf/push --force/chmod 777; correlation tag is plain ASCII).

Verdict is CONTEST rather than PASS on two medium-severity quality concerns that warrant an author response: (1) a session-vs-subprocess model-resolution asymmetry where an inherited model id that is not resolvable through a freshly-created, NON-network-refreshed `ModelRuntime` catalog is silently DROPPED on the session backend while the subprocess backend honors it unconditionally — so the headline Feature-1 acceptance ("every spawned specialist on BOTH backends uses that model") can quietly fail on the session backend with zero signal; and (2) an undocumented global render-validation semantics change in `validateData` (silently dropping ALL "must not have additional properties" errors, not just for strict-capable schemas) that broadens beyond the feature's stated scope and is absent from the CHANGELOG's "byte-identical fallback" claims. Neither risks production failure, data loss, or security breach (both degrade no-throw / gracefully), so REJECT is not warranted. Test coverage for the new precedence tiers, `isStrictCapable` gating, and build-correlation is solid and the mocking strategy is sound (vi.hoisted + vi.mock of the SDK and ModelRuntime).

findings.title: Session-backend inherited model is silently dropped if absent from a non-network-refreshed ModelRuntime catalog — diverges from subprocess backend
findings.detail: Feature 1's acceptance requires that BOTH backends use the live session's model when no override is supplied. The subprocess backend (`buildSpawnArgs`, src/pi-spawn.ts ~resolveModel/buildSpawnArgs) passes the raw inherited id to `--model` UNCONDITIONALLY and lets pi's CLI resolve it. The session backend (`resolveSessionModel`, src/session-agent.ts) instead resolves the id against `ModelRuntime.create()` and, per the verified 0.82.1 d.ts, that class's `create()` defaults `allowNetworkRefresh` to FALSE — so the catalog it scans is the bundled one, NOT the user's provider-configured catalog. If `ctx.model.id` is a custom-provider / OpenAI-compatible / settings-configured model the bundled catalog doesn't know, `resolveSessionModel` returns undefined and `createAgentSession` omits `model`, falling through to the SDK/settings default. The subprocess backend honors the inherited id; the session backend silently does not — a divergence from 'every specialist on BOTH backends uses that model' with NO observable signal (the no-throw fall-through is intentional and correct for robustness, but masks the divergence). Mitigations: (a) when an inherited id is supplied but fails catalog resolution, emit a one-line best-effort `ctx.log`/progress note so the divergence is observable; or (b) fall back to passing a minimal `{ id }` descriptor to `createAgentSession` (the SDK may still resolve it via settings, which often equals the right model anyway). At minimum, document the asymmetry and the `allowNetworkRefresh=false` assumption in the comment block on `resolveSessionModel`. Tagged UNCERTAIN on real-world blast radius because the settings-default fall-through frequently coincides with the correct model.

findings.title: validateData now silently drops ALL additional-properties errors globally — undocumented render-validation semantics change
findings.detail: src/render/render.ts `validateData` adds `if (e.message === "must not have additional properties") continue;` for EVERY schema, gated only by a comment, not by `isStrictCapable`. This was necessitated by closing the review/implementation schemas (additionalProperties:false) in src/render/schemas.ts so strict constrained-sampling works, but it removes a general render-validation guarantee: any FUTURE or OTHER schema that intentionally sets `additionalProperties: false` to ENFORCE no-extra-keys at render time will silently stop enforcing it, and a model emitting junk keys into such a schema will render instead of failing its gate. The CHANGELOG's Feature-2 bullet claims the non-capable/permissive path is 'PRESERVED byte-identical' — that is true for the structured_output/missingKeys path, but render validation semantics changed globally and that change is not mentioned. Recommend: scope the tolerance to strict-capable schemas (skip the error only when `isStrictCapable(schema)` is true, OR only for schemas explicitly marked as the constrained-sampling variant), and add a line to the CHANGELOG noting the deliberate global change. If the intent really is global, make that explicit in the comment rather than framing it as a strict-capable-only accommodation.

findings.title: Session backend couples to a fresh ModelRuntime catalog subsystem, duplicating resolution logic the SDK/settings layer already owns
findings.detail: To thread `model?: Model<any>`, Feature 1 introduces `getModelRuntime`, `splitModelRef`, `resolveSessionModel`, and a process-wide `runtimeCache` (src/session-agent.ts) that reach into pi's `ModelRuntime` catalog and do provider-splitting + full-catalog scans. The spec envisioned 'pass the resolved model via the SDK's model option'; this implementation owns model resolution end-to-end instead. It is correct and no-throw, but it is a meaningfully larger surface than required and must track pi's catalog/resolution evolution. If `createAgentSession` ever accepts a bare id (or resolves a `{id}` descriptor via settings — which is what its own default path does), most of this subsystem collapses. Consider whether a minimal descriptor + settings fall-through would reduce coupling; if keeping the catalog approach, isolate the resolution so a single pi API change doesn't ripple. No production risk; flagged as coupling cost.

findings.title: Process-wide mutable runtimeCache has no invalidation hook — test isolation & long-session staleness
findings.detail: `let runtimeCache: Promise<ModelRuntime> | undefined` (src/session-agent.ts) is module-level and keyed to nothing; it is created once per process and shared across every session-backend spawn. The inherit tests correctly vi.mock `ModelRuntime` (tests/session-agent-inherit.test.ts:65-80) so they don't hit it, but any future test path that lets `ModelRuntime.create()` run for real will cache a live runtime for the whole vitest process, and a long-lived TUI session that changes providers/settings mid-run will keep the stale catalog (compounding F-1's `allowNetworkRefresh=false` behavior). The rejection-clear-on-failure retry logic is good. Minor; consider a reset hook for tests and a comment on the no-mid-run-invalidation assumption.

findings.title: Inline doc comments over-reference internal AC-NN/SCENARIO-NNN/F-N/AR-NN tracking codes future maintainers lack the key for
findings.detail: Nearly every added/edited function carries a multi-paragraph comment citing SCENARIO-001/005/008, F-1/F-2, AR-02/AR-03, AC-04/AC-10, etc. This is consistent with the repo's existing house style (the surrounding code is equally verbose), so it is not a defect, but a minimalist lens flags that for a feature set this size the scenario-code cross-references add volume that adds little maintenance value once the spec directory is archived. Intent-first prose ('inherited wins over role default, loses to env/per-call') would carry the same information. No action required; noted for consistency-of-style awareness.

findings.title: Double-application guard is correct but split across two modules — invariant rests on a single truthy-check
findings.detail: The 'do not double-apply thinking' guarantee (SCENARIO-007) depends on `resolveExplicitThinking` (pi-spawn.ts, no role default) returning truthy exactly when an override exists, which then gates `if (!creationThinking) applyThinkingLevel(session, resolveThinking(...))` in runAgentViaSession. The logic is correct and is pinned by an existing invariant test ('session.setThinkingLevel is never called more than once for a single run', tests/session-agent-inherit.test.ts:164). No action — flagged only so the cross-module invariant is preserved during any future refactor of resolveExplicitThinking/resolveThinking's return semantics.

data.title: Code Review — spec-15: pi Integration Modernization (model/thinking inheritance, constrained structured_output sampling, typed registerEntryRenderer, build session-env tagging)
data.summary:
All five features are implemented cohesively and match the detailed precedence/contract spec. Verified: `npm run typecheck` is strict-clean against the 0.82.1 type surface; targeted vitest suites for inheritance (pi-spawn), constrained sampling, and build correlation pass (72/72); the `registerEntryRenderer` `as unknown as` capability cast is deleted and replaced with a typed `pi.registerEntryRenderer(...)` call (the remaining `as unknown as` occurrences are all in tests or unrelated render-error narrowing). Dimension scores: Correctness 4/5, Security 5/5, Performance 4/5, Concurrency 4/5, Maintainability 4/5, Testability 5/5, Error Handling 5/5, Data Integrity 4/5, Observability 5/5.

Feature 1 (highest leverage): `ctx.model?.id` / `ctx.thinkingLevel` are captured defensively in `extension.execute()` before `runPipelineTask`, threaded as additive `inheritedModel`/`inheritedThinking` DEFAULTS through `RunOptions → realAgent.common → both backends`. `resolveThinking` precedence is correctly widened (per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING → INHERITED → role default); `resolveModel` adds the NEW SUPER_DEV_MODEL tier (explicit → env → inherited → SDK default); `--model` is pushed only when a model resolves. The session backend passes `model` + `thinkingLevel` as `createAgentSession` options alongside a retained `applyThinkingLevel`, with a clean double-application guard (`if (!creationThinking) applyThinkingLevel(...)`). Model-id resolution no-throws and falls through to the SDK/settings default when the catalog can't resolve it (SCENARIO-008). Older/non-TUI ctx degrades byte-identically. AC-01..05 / SCENARIO-001..008 met.

Feature 2: `isStrictCapable(schema)` correctly returns true ONLY for a typebox Object with `additionalProperties === false` (exact `!== false` check, so undefined/true permissive schemas are excluded) AND ≥1 required non-Optional key. `constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` is attached to the `structured_output` ToolDefinition solely on that gate; the all-Optional `controlSchema` + `missingKeys()` + single corrective re-prompt are preserved byte-identical as the fallback. Only the review/implementation stage schemas (SpecReview/CodeReview/AdversarialReview/ImplementationSummary + nested Finding/dimensions) were closed to be strict-capable; the remaining stage schemas stay permissive → byte-identical. AC-06..08 / SCENARIO-009..013 met.

Feature 3: renderer registered via the typed public API; best-effort try/catch retained. Feature 4: `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_MODEL` read defensively (try-guarded against a hostile `process.env` proxy), omitted entirely when both absent (byte-identical), and emitted as a plain-ASCII `# pi-session=… model=…` line to the run trace at all three build-gate sites plus an additive `correlation` field on `BuildGateResult`. No pass/fail/command/timeout change. AC-10 / SCENARIO-016..017 met. Feature 5: CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry present in Keep-a-Changelog style covering Features 1–4 + the already-committed bump. AC-11 / SCENARIO-018 met.

No Critical or High issues. Three Low-severity items below (one spec-clarification, one intentional validation weakening worth confirming, one minor inefficiency) — none block approval.

findings.title: Spec ambiguity: "no lower than role default" vs implemented pure inherited-wins precedence
findings.detail: Feature 1's acceptance says spawned specialists use "a thinking level no LOWER than the role default would have been (inherited wins over role default…)". These two clauses conflict when an inherited level is LOWER than a role default — e.g. a reasoning role (code-reviewer/adversarial-reviewer/design/spec-writer, default "high") inheriting "medium"/"low"/"minimal" from the main session. The implementation (`resolveThinking`/`resolveExplicitThinking` in src/pi-spawn.ts and the `creationThinking` path in src/session-agent.ts) follows the MORE detailed/explicit precedence chain in the Feature 1 body (per-call → SUPER_DEV_THINKING → INHERITED → role default) with pure replacement and NO max-floor, so such a role will think BELOW its role default. This is a defensible reading (the user explicitly chose a low level for their session and inheritance is the feature), and matches the detailed precedence spec, but if the "no lower" intent was real the reasoning-heavy stages could regress on quality. Failure scenario: user runs `/super-dev` from a session pinned to `low` thinking → code-reviewer/adversarial-reviewer think at `low` instead of `high`, weakening the review loop. Suggested fix: confirm with the spec author which clause is authoritative; if a floor is intended, resolve the effective level as `max(inherited, thinkingForAgent(agent))` (via the THINKING_LEVELS ordinal) instead of pure replacement. Confidence 0.6 (UNCERTAIN — genuinely spec-ambiguous).

findings.title: Render validator now silently swallows additionalProperties errors (intentional, but a gate weakening)
findings.detail: `validateData` in src/render/render.ts adds `if (e.message === "must not have additional properties") continue;`, so any schema with `additionalProperties:false` no longer fails the render/gate when the agent over-fills it. The rationale (strict-capable review/implementation schemas carry that flag for constrained sampling, and templates only render declared keys) is sound and the change is documented, but it applies UNCONDITIONALLY to every closed schema regardless of provider capability. On a non-capable provider (glm/local) where `strict:"prefer"` is not enforced, an agent returning extra keys on e.g. CodeReviewData now passes validation silently rather than surfacing as a gate error. Practical impact is low because templates ignore extras and downstream consumers read only declared keys, and required-key/type errors are still reported — but it is a net reduction in the gate's signal. Suggested fix: keep the swallow (it is needed) but consider also emitting a debug-level notice when an additionalProperties violation is dropped, so the gate retains observability without failing. Confidence 0.7.

findings.title: missingKeys() checks prompt-extracted keys while constrained sampling enforces schema-required keys — can spuriously fire the corrective re-prompt
findings.detail: In `structuredOutputTool`, the tool description and the `missingKeys()` corrective-re-prompt gate use `keys` (prompt-extracted via `extractControlKeys`), while `constrainedSampling` (when attached) constrains the SCHEMA's required keys. For strict-capable stages these two key sets can diverge (e.g. the prompt lists `title,date,verdict,summary,findings` but the schema also requires nested Finding `id/severity/title/detail`). On a capable provider the model is forced to fill all schema-required keys, yet `missingKeys()` may still report a prompt-declared key as missing and trigger the corrective turn — slightly contradicting AC-07's "corrective re-prompt should rarely fire" on capable providers. Harmless (the corrective re-prompt is a safe no-op that just asks for the already-present object again) but wasteful. Suggested fix: when `isStrictCapable(effective)` holds, derive the `missingKeys` check from the schema's `required` array instead of the prompt-extracted keys (or union them). Confidence 0.6.

findings.title: Module-level ModelRuntime cache is process-wide; correct for production, note for test isolation
findings.detail: `getModelRuntime()` caches `ModelRuntime.create()` at module scope (cleared only on rejection). This is correct for production (the model catalog is immutable per process and shared across every session-backend spawn, avoiding per-spawn catalog cost), but it means tests that exercise `resolveSessionModel` share one real catalog unless the cache is reset. No production bug; flagging only so future test authors know to clear `runtimeCache` or mock at a higher seam if they need deterministic catalog behavior. Confidence 0.8.
